=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel – Buyer-side review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter

**To:** Wattlebridge deal team  **From:** AI legal assistant  **Date:** 5 November 2026

## 0. Threshold point: do not accept the Seller's framing

Before the substance, three things in the Seller's package should be disregarded or challenged outright:

1. **The "[STANDARD] / FINAL / cleared by both sides / review only [OPEN]" labels.** Nothing in the package is marked [OPEN], so taken literally the instruction is "review nothing". These labels are the Seller's assertions, not an agreed record. Unless *our* principals confirm in writing that specific positions were agreed, every clause remains open. I have reviewed all of them below. Please check with the Wattlebridge principals whether anything was in fact conceded at principal level – if not, the covering letter should say so expressly to avoid an "agreed in principle" argument later.
2. **The "market context" preamble.** It is Seller-authored and self-serving. Some of the ranges are within the spread seen in Australian mid-market private M&A, but it omits that the *lower* ends apply where W&I insurance is in place or the target is clean. Here the Seller's own Disclosure Letter identifies at least six live problems. That argues for the buyer-favourable end, not the seller end.
3. **The Disclosure Letter is dated 22 September 2026 – six weeks stale.** Several items (Bluefen consent, Riverlark payoff, the DD-006 investigation) are time-sensitive. Require a bring-down disclosure at signing and again at Completion, with any new matter giving a termination right, not just further "disclosure".

Note also the internal inconsistency: the Seller Update describes positions as "settled", while clause 11 of the Disclosure Letter says "no … negotiation position or approval is included" and that the Buyer "must evaluate the disclosed facts" itself. We should hold the Seller to the latter.

---

## 1. Limitation package (cl 12, 13, 9.3, 12.8, 20.5, 8.3)

### 1.1 General cap – 20% (AUD 4.8m)
Not unreasonable in isolation for *general* warranties, but only if (a) it is genuinely confined to general warranties and (b) the deal is otherwise clean. Given the identified issues, open at **50%**, settle no lower than **30%** unless W&I insurance is procured (in which case 20% or even lower is fine, provided the retention is funded by Seller).

### 1.2 Fundamental, title, capacity – "same caps and time limits for administrative simplicity"
**Reject.** This is well outside any market. Title and capacity warranties must be capped at **100% of price** (or uncapped) and run for the maximum limitation period (6 years in NSW, or 7 years in deeds). If title fails, "administrative simplicity" means Wattlebridge paid AUD 24m for nothing and can recover AUD 4.8m.

### 1.3 Tax and IP – "settled under the general regime"
**Reject.** Separate regimes required:
- **Tax:** full tax indemnity for pre-Completion tax (not just warranties), capped at 100% of price, surviving until 4 years after expiry of the Commissioner's amendment period (in practice **7 years**). For a SaaS business, specifically cover R&D Tax Incentive claims, Division 7A, employee share scheme reporting and payroll tax on contractors.
- **IP:** a SaaS business *is* its IP. IP warranties should sit at a higher cap (at least 50%, ideally 100%) and a longer period (3 years+). See also Ironquay at §3.3 – the IP title problem is already known.

### 1.4 De minimis AUD 25k / basket AUD 250k, "only the excess" recoverable
- De minimis of ~0.1% of price is acceptable. Ensure **related claims aggregate** so the Seller cannot slice one issue into sub-25k pieces (see the Sandbar point at §3.6 – three invoices of exactly AUD 110k is precisely the pattern to guard against).
- The basket is drafted as a **deductible**. Push for a **tipping basket** (once exceeded, recover from the first dollar). If a deductible is the price of a lower basket, counter with a lower figure.
- Thresholds must **not** apply to fundamental/title warranties, tax, specific indemnities, leakage/debt-like adjustments or covenant breaches.

### 1.5 Time limits – 18 months, and "applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise"
- 18 months for general warranties is at the short end. Push for **24 months** (two financial year-ends and audit cycles, which is where accounting and revenue-recognition issues surface in SaaS – deferred revenue, ARR definitions, churn).
- Ensure the clause requires **notification** within the period and gives at least **6–9 months after notification** to commence proceedings; otherwise claims notified late in the window lapse immediately.
- The "all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" default must be **reversed**: limitations apply *only* to general Warranty Claims and nothing else unless expressly stated. This single drafting default, if accepted, drags every indemnity, covenant, completion-accounts dispute and tax claim into the 18-month/20% box.

### 1.6 Cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 – limitations, exclusive remedy, non-reliance "apply to all Claims of any nature"
**Reject in that form.** Required carve-outs: fraud, dishonesty, wilful concealment or wilful misconduct; specific indemnities; tax indemnity; fundamental/title warranties; price adjustment / completion accounts / leakage; restraint, confidentiality and other post-Completion covenants; and the Seller's own obligations at Completion (e.g. Riverlark discharge). Also note that under the ACL, misleading or deceptive conduct liability cannot be contracted out of – a sweeping non-reliance clause will be read down and is better narrowed to a defensible statement of what was and was not relied on.

### 1.7 Cl 8.3 – Buyer knowledge, including advisers' knowledge and anything "discoverable" from data room or public records
**Reject.** This is the single most dangerous clause in the package. Combined with general disclosure (§2), it means: every matter in the data room is disclosed *and* deemed known, so no warranty claim can ever succeed on anything the Seller put in the data room, including the six known problems. Constructive knowledge ("discoverable") and imputed adviser knowledge are not acceptable. Maximum concession: no claim for matters within the **actual knowledge of named individuals** on the Wattlebridge deal team, *and* only to the extent fairly disclosed. Better position: delete entirely and rely on the disclosure standard.

---

## 2. Disclosure framework (Sch 7, Disclosure Letter cl 1)

The Seller "relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers". **Reject** general disclosure. Required position:

- Disclosure is effective only if **fair, specific, and with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter** and its likely effect on the Company. A document buried in the data room does not disclose a problem that is not apparent on its face.
- Data room disclosure limited to documents **listed in an agreed index**, cross-referenced to the specific warranty they qualify, on a USB/fixed copy annexed to the SPA.
- Public registers limited to **ASIC company extract and PPSR** against the Company as at a named date (not "publicly searchable corporate records" generally, and no court lists, IP Australia, etc. unless specifically searched and annexed).
- **No disclosure** against fundamental/title warranties or against specific indemnities.
- Clause 1.4 (non-admission) is fine as a non-admission but must not be read as a reservation that disclosed matters are *not* disclosed; add that the Buyer's acceptance of disclosure is likewise without admission that the matter is immaterial.

Observation: the Disclosure Letter is unusually candid about what the Seller has **not** done (no Bluefen consent, no Riverlark discharge, no Ironquay receipt, no incident assessment). That candour is useful – it establishes the Seller's knowledge – but under the Seller's framework it also converts each of those gaps into a *disclosed, unclaimable* matter. Hence every item below needs a **specific indemnity or completion deliverable**, not a warranty.

---

## 3. Specific commercial / diligence issues

### 3.1 Bluefen (DD-002) – ~AUD 3.6m revenue, ~30% of FY26; consent not obtained
The Seller offers "reasonable endeavours" and deems the CP satisfied "on delivery of the counterparty's written consent". Problems: (a) clause 11.3 attaches **conditions** to consent – a bare letter may not satisfy them; (b) "reasonable endeavours" with no deadline; (c) no protection if Bluefen consents then terminates or re-prices.

Push for:
- Hard CP for **Buyer's benefit only** (waivable by Buyer): unconditional written consent in a form approved by Buyer, with all 11.3 conditions satisfied or waived by Bluefen in writing, and no amendment to pricing, term or scope.
- Seller to use **best** (or at least "all reasonable") endeavours, with Buyer entitled to participate in discussions.
- If Bluefen terminates or gives notice within 12 months post-Completion, a **price adjustment or retention release** mechanism (e.g. retention of 2–3x Bluefen annual gross margin). At minimum a specific indemnity if the termination is linked to the change of control.

### 3.2 Riverlark Bank (DD-003) – AUD 3.2m, release "following Completion"
**Not acceptable on a debt-free/cash-free deal.** Clause 8.1 is a change-of-control trigger, so the facility goes into default the moment we complete without consent; clause 9.2 governs discharge. If release follows Completion, Wattlebridge buys a defaulted, secured borrower and relies on an unsecured post-Completion covenant from a venture vehicle.

Require as **Completion deliverables**: payoff letter from Riverlark stating the exact discharge amount; repayment at Completion out of the purchase price via the funds flow; executed deed of release and PPSR discharge (or irrevocable undertaking to register discharge within 2 business days); release of any guarantees or security given by the Company. Confirm whether Riverlark holds a **share mortgage over the Paperbark shares** – if so, release is a title issue, not just a debt issue. Riverlark amount must appear as a debt-like item in the price mechanics.

### 3.3 Ironquay Development Studio (DD-004 / DD-010) – SOW3 IP conditional on payment; AUD 180k unpaid
Under cl 7.3 the Company **does not own the SOW3 Project Materials** until every SOW3 fee is paid. The Seller's indemnity "limited to the specific SOW3 payment" covers AUD 180k and nothing else. If SOW3 materials are in the production codebase, the real exposure is loss of title to part of the product, infringement claims, licence-back costs and re-engineering – multiples of 180k.

Push for: (a) CP / Completion deliverable: evidence of cleared payment and a **confirmatory deed of assignment** from Ironquay, including moral rights consents; or (b) Buyer pays AUD 180k from the price directly to Ironquay at Completion against the assignment; plus (c) a **specific indemnity** covering all loss arising from any defect in title to Ironquay-developed IP, uncapped or capped at price, outside the basket. Ask DD to confirm whether SOW1–2 were paid and assigned.

### 3.4 Completion bonuses (DD-005) – AUD 420k, not in funds flow
The Seller says this is "a matter for the Seller" – good – but the funds flow does not reflect it, and the bonuses are **Company** liabilities triggered by Completion. Under debt-free/cash-free they are debt-like items. Also unquantified: superannuation (12% from 1 July 2025), NSW payroll tax (~5.45%), leave accruals impact, PAYG withholding – total cost closer to **AUD 495k**.

Push for: the gross bonuses **plus all on-costs** either (i) deducted from the price as a debt-like item or (ii) paid by the Company at Completion out of funds the Seller provides, with a specific indemnity for any shortfall. Because the bonuses have continued-employment conditions, some may fall due post-Completion – they must still be Seller-funded. Confirm no further "change of control" payments under employment contracts or any ESOP acceleration.

### 3.5 DD-006 data export – ~1,240 personal records sent to wrong external address
The Seller calls this "preliminary" and "not expected to be material". Our view: it is a potential **eligible data breach** under the Notifiable Data Breaches scheme (Privacy Act Part IIIC). The Company is obliged to complete its assessment within 30 days of becoming aware – the incident is pre-22 September, so that window has likely **already expired**. Exposure includes OAIC regulatory action (penalties now up to the greater of AUD 50m / 3x benefit / 30% turnover for serious interferences), the statutory tort for serious invasions of privacy (in force since June 2025), customer contract breach-notification obligations (check Bluefen and Mossvale contracts), and reputational damage to a data-analytics business.

Push for: (a) completed written assessment and legal advice **before signing**, including whether the recipient confirmed deletion; (b) a covenant to notify OAIC and affected individuals if required, with Buyer consultation rights and no public statements without Buyer approval; (c) a **specific indemnity**, outside the cap and basket, for all loss, fines, notification costs, third-party claims and customer remediation arising from the incident; (d) if assessment is not completed, a CP or a retention.

### 3.6 Sandbar renewals (DD-008 / DD-011) – 3 × AUD 110k = AUD 330k
"Ordinary-course operating costs" is asserted, not evidenced. The Disclosure Letter itself says it does not state whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. Three identical amounts, documented across two separate DD references, look structured to sit under the de minimis individually. Require: copies of the renewal terms; confirmation whether committed pre-Completion for post-Completion periods (if so, treat as debt-like/prepayment adjustment or Seller cost); gap-period covenant requiring Buyer consent for any commitment over, say, AUD 50k; and aggregation language for related claims (see §1.4).

### 3.7 Title (DD-012) – share register only
A share register is prima facie evidence, not proof. Before signing: current ASIC extract; constitution (pre-emption rights, transfer restrictions); share certificates or confirmation none issued; confirmation of no options, SAFEs, convertible notes, warrants or ESOP interests (common in venture-backed SaaS – Harbourglass is a "Ventures" entity); PPSR search against Seller and Company for share security; any shareholders' agreement. Title warranty uncapped, no disclosure against it (§1.2, §2).

### 3.8 Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)
Lower risk but confirm. Lease: obtain the clause; if notification only, add a Seller covenant to give notice pre-Completion and warrant no landlord consent or CoC termination right. Mossvale: an anti-assignment clause is not usually triggered by a share sale, but check for a separately defined change-of-control provision and any "key person" or ownership-based termination right; obtain a warranty that no customer or supplier contract (above a threshold) contains CoC rights other than those listed.

---

## 4. Structural protections the package omits entirely

- **Covenant strength / security for claims.** Harbourglass Ventures is a venture vehicle likely to distribute proceeds promptly. Without security, every warranty and indemnity above is only as good as the Seller's post-Completion balance sheet. Require a **retention/escrow** (e.g. 10–15% of price for 24 months, stepping down) or a parent/fund guarantee. W&I insurance is the alternative, and would also legitimately unlock the lower cap the Seller wants.
- **Completion accounts / locked box.** The package refers to "agreed price mechanics" without specifying. Confirm which mechanism applies and that Riverlark, bonuses (+ on-costs), Ironquay AUD 180k and any Sandbar prepayments are expressly listed as debt-like / leakage items.
- **Material adverse change / termination right** between signing and Completion, given Bluefen and the DD-006 incident.
- **Gap covenants** restricting conduct of business, new commitments and any dealing with Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay or the regulator without Buyer consent.
- **Restraints** on Harbourglass and key principals – not mentioned anywhere in the Seller package.

---

## 5. Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Seller position | Recommended Buyer position | Priority |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | "[STANDARD]/FINAL" framing | Review only [OPEN] items | Reject; confirm with principals nothing is agreed; all open | Immediate |
| 2 | Fundamental/title/capacity | Same cap and 18 months | 100% of price, 6–7 years, no disclosure against | Must-have |
| 3 | Tax & IP | General regime | Separate tax indemnity (100%, 7 yrs); IP at ≥50% cap, 3 yrs | Must-have |
| 4 | General cap | 20% | Open 50%, floor 30% (or 20% with W&I) | High |
| 5 | Basket | Deductible, 1% | Tipping basket; exclude indemnities/fundamental/tax | High |
| 6 | Time limits | 18 months, all claims | 24 months general; limitations apply only to general warranty claims; 6–9 months to sue after notice | High |
| 7 | Exclusive remedy / non-reliance | All claims | Carve out fraud, indemnities, tax, title, price adjustment, covenants | Must-have |
| 8 | Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3) | Incl. advisers & "discoverable" | Delete; max concession actual knowledge of named individuals | Must-have |
| 9 | Disclosure | General data room + public records | Fair & specific disclosure only; indexed data room; ASIC/PPSR only; none against fundamental/indemnities | Must-have |
| 10 | Bluefen | Reasonable endeavours, deemed satisfied on letter | Hard Buyer CP, unconditional consent incl. 11.3, retention/price protection | Must-have |
| 11 | Riverlark | Release after Completion | Payoff letter, repayment from price and release/PPSR discharge **at** Completion | Must-have |
| 12 | Ironquay | Indemnity for AUD 180k only | Payment + confirmatory assignment at Completion; broad IP indemnity | Must-have |
| 13 | Bonuses | Not in funds flow | AUD 420k + on-costs as debt-like item / Seller-funded, with indemnity | High |
| 14 | DD-006 incident | "Not material" | Completed assessment pre-signing; notification covenant; uncapped specific indemnity | High |
| 15 | Sandbar | Ordinary course | Evidence; treat committed post-Completion costs as debt-like; aggregation language | Medium |
| 16 | Title evidence | Share register | Full verification; no options/convertibles warranty | High |
| 17 | Lease / Mossvale | Notification only / no consent | Verify clauses; covenants and CoC warranty | Medium |
| 18 | Security for claims | None | Escrow 10–15% / guarantee, or W&I | Must-have |
| 19 | Stale disclosure | Dated 22 Sep 2026 | Bring-down at signing and Completion with termination right | High |

**Bottom line:** the limitation package is drafted so that the Seller's own disclosed problems – a 30%-of-revenue customer consent not obtained, AUD 3.2m of secured debt not discharged, IP the Company does not yet own, AUD 420k+ of Completion-triggered liabilities, and a potentially notifiable privacy breach – would all be disclosed, deemed known, and either unclaimable or subject to a 20% cap and 18-month tail. Each of those items needs to be converted into a Completion deliverable, price adjustment or specific indemnity sitting outside the general regime, and the general regime itself needs the carve-outs above. I would recommend the covering response state plainly that Wattlebridge does not accept the pre-categorisation and treats every clause as open.

Happy to turn this into a clause-by-clause mark-up or a shorter issues list for the principals' call.

### 1.6 Cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 – limitations, exclusive remedy, non-reliance "apply to all Claims of any nature"
**Reject in that form.** Required carve-outs: fraud, dishonesty, wilful concealment or wilful misconduct; specific indemnities; tax indemnity; fundamental/title warranties; price adjustment / completion accounts / leakage; restraint, confidentiality and other post-Completion covenants; and the Seller's own obligations at Completion (e.g. Riverlark discharge). Also note that under the ACL, misleading or deceptive conduct liability cannot be contracted out of – a sweeping non-reliance clause will be read down and is better narrowed to a defensible statement of what was and was not relied on.

### 1.7 Cl 8.3 – Buyer knowledge, including advisers' knowledge and anything "discoverable" from data room or public records
**Reject.** This is the single most dangerous clause in the package. Combined with general disclosure (§2), it means: every matter in the data room is disclosed *and* deemed known, so no warranty claim can ever succeed on anything the Seller put in the data room, including the six known problems. Constructive knowledge ("discoverable") and imputed adviser knowledge are not acceptable. Maximum concession: no claim for matters within the **actual knowledge of named individuals** on the Wattlebridge deal team, *and* only to the extent fairly disclosed. Better position: delete entirely and rely on the disclosure standard.

## 2. Disclosure framework (Sch 7, Disclosure Letter cl 1)

The Seller "relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers". **Reject** general disclosure. Required position:

- Disclosure is effective only if **fair, specific, and with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter** and its likely effect on the Company. A document buried in the data room does not disclose a problem that is not apparent on its face.
- Data room disclosure limited to documents **listed in an agreed index**, cross-referenced to the specific warranty they qualify, on a USB/fixed copy annexed to the SPA.
- Public registers limited to **ASIC company extract and PPSR** against the Company as at a named date (not "publicly searchable corporate records" generally, and no court lists, IP Australia, etc. unless specifically searched and annexed).
- **No disclosure** against fundamental/title warranties or against specific indemnities.
- Clause 1.4 (non-admission) is fine as a non-admission but must not be read as a reservation that disclosed matters are *not* disclosed; add that the Buyer's acceptance of disclosure is likewise without admission that the matter is immaterial.

Observation: the Disclosure Letter is unusually candid about what the Seller has **not** done (no Bluefen consent, no Riverlark discharge, no Ironquay receipt, no incident assessment). That candour is useful – it establishes the Seller's knowledge – but under the Seller's framework it also converts each of those gaps into a *disclosed, unclaimable* matter. Hence every item below needs a **specific indemnity or completion deliverable**, not a warranty.

## 3. Specific commercial / diligence issues

### 3.1 Bluefen (DD-002) – ~AUD 3.6m revenue, ~30% of FY26; consent not obtained
The Seller offers "reasonable endeavours" and deems the CP satisfied "on delivery of the counterparty's written consent". Problems: (a) clause 11.3 attaches **conditions** to consent – a bare letter may not satisfy them; (b) "reasonable endeavours" with no deadline; (c) no protection if Bluefen consents then terminates or re-prices.

Push for:
- Hard CP for **Buyer's benefit only** (waivable by Buyer): unconditional written consent in a form approved by Buyer, with all 11.3 conditions satisfied or waived by Bluefen in writing, and no amendment to pricing, term or scope.
- Seller to use **best** (or at least "all reasonable") endeavours, with Buyer entitled to participate in discussions.
- If Bluefen terminates or gives notice within 12 months post-Completion, a **price adjustment or retention release** mechanism (e.g. retention of 2–3x Bluefen annual gross margin). At minimum a specific indemnity if the termination is linked to the change of control.

### 3.2 Riverlark Bank (DD-003) – AUD 3.2m, release "following Completion"
**Not acceptable on a debt-free/cash-free deal.** Clause 8.1 is a change-of-control trigger, so the facility goes into default the moment we complete without consent; clause 9.2 governs discharge. If release follows Completion, Wattlebridge buys a defaulted, secured borrower and relies on an unsecured post-Completion covenant from a venture vehicle.

Require as **Completion deliverables**: payoff letter from Riverlark stating the exact discharge amount; repayment at Completion out of the purchase price via the funds flow; executed deed of release and PPSR discharge (or irrevocable undertaking to register discharge within 2 business days); release of any guarantees or security given by the Company. Confirm whether Riverlark holds a **share mortgage over the Paperbark shares** – if so, release is a title issue, not just a debt issue. Riverlark amount must appear as a debt-like item in the price mechanics.

### 3.3 Ironquay Development Studio (DD-004 / DD-010) – SOW3 IP conditional on payment; AUD 180k unpaid
Under cl 7.3 the Company **does not own the SOW3 Project Materials** until every SOW3 fee is paid. The Seller's indemnity "limited to the specific SOW3 payment" covers AUD 180k and nothing else. If SOW3 materials are in the production codebase, the real exposure is loss of title to part of the product, infringement claims, licence-back costs and re-engineering – multiples of 180k.

Push for: (a) CP / Completion deliverable: evidence of cleared payment and a **confirmatory deed of assignment** from Ironquay, including moral rights consents; or (b) Buyer pays AUD 180k from the price directly to Ironquay at Completion against the assignment; plus (c) a **specific indemnity** covering all loss arising from any defect in title to Ironquay-developed IP, uncapped or capped at price, outside the basket. Ask DD to confirm whether SOW1–2 were paid and assigned.

### 3.4 Completion bonuses (DD-005) – AUD 420k, not in funds flow
The Seller says this is "a matter for the Seller" – good – but the funds flow does not reflect it, and the bonuses are **Company** liabilities triggered by Completion. Under debt-free/cash-free they are debt-like items. Also unquantified: superannuation (12% from 1 July 2025), NSW payroll tax (~5.45%), leave accruals impact, PAYG withholding – total cost closer to **AUD 495k**.

Push for: the gross bonuses **plus all on-costs** either (i) deducted from the price as a debt-like item or (ii) paid by the Company at Completion out of funds the Seller provides, with a specific indemnity for any shortfall. Because the bonuses have continued-employment conditions, some may fall due post-Completion – they must still be Seller-funded. Confirm no further "change of control" payments under employment contracts or any ESOP acceleration.

### 3.5 DD-006 data export – ~1,240 personal records sent to wrong external address
The Seller calls this "preliminary" and "not expected to be material". Our view: it is a potential **eligible data breach** under the Notifiable Data Breaches scheme (Privacy Act Part IIIC). The Company is obliged to complete its assessment within 30 days of becoming aware – the incident is pre-22 September, so that window has likely **already expired**. Exposure includes OAIC regulatory action (penalties now up to the greater of AUD 50m / 3x benefit / 30% turnover for serious interferences), the statutory tort for serious invasions of privacy (in force since June 2025), customer contract breach-notification obligations (check Bluefen and Mossvale contracts), and reputational damage to a data-analytics business.

Push for: (a) completed written assessment and legal advice **before signing**, including whether the recipient confirmed deletion; (b) a covenant to notify OAIC and affected individuals if required, with Buyer consultation rights and no public statements without Buyer approval; (c) a **specific indemnity**, outside the cap and basket, for all loss, fines, notification costs, third-party claims and customer remediation arising from the incident; (d) if assessment is not completed, a CP or a retention.

### 3.6 Sandbar renewals (DD-008 / DD-011) – 3 × AUD 110k = AUD 330k
"Ordinary-course operating costs" is asserted, not evidenced. The Disclosure Letter itself says it does not state whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. Three identical amounts, documented across two separate DD references, look structured to sit under the de minimis individually. Require: copies of the renewal terms; confirmation whether committed pre-Completion for post-Completion periods (if so, treat as debt-like/prepayment adjustment or Seller cost); gap-period covenant requiring Buyer consent for any commitment over, say, AUD 50k; and aggregation language for related claims (see §1.4).

### 3.7 Title (DD-012) – share register only
A share register is prima facie evidence, not proof. Before signing: current ASIC extract; constitution (pre-emption rights, transfer restrictions); share certificates or confirmation none issued; confirmation of no options, SAFEs, convertible notes, warrants or ESOP interests (common in venture-backed SaaS – Harbourglass is a "Ventures" entity); PPSR search against Seller and Company for share security; any shareholders' agreement. Title warranty uncapped, no disclosure against it (§1.2, §2).

### 3.8 Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)
Lower risk but confirm. Lease: obtain the clause; if notification only, add a Seller covenant to give notice pre-Completion and warrant no landlord consent or CoC termination right. Mossvale: an anti-assignment clause is not usually triggered by a share sale, but check for a separately defined change-of-control provision and any "key person" or ownership-based termination right; obtain a warranty that no customer or supplier contract (above a threshold) contains CoC rights other than those listed.

## 4. Structural protections the package omits entirely

- **Covenant strength / security for claims.** Harbourglass Ventures is a venture vehicle likely to distribute proceeds promptly. Without security, every warranty and indemnity above is only as good as the Seller's post-Completion balance sheet. Require a **retention/escrow** (e.g. 10–15% of price for 24 months, stepping down) or a parent/fund guarantee. W&I insurance is the alternative, and would also legitimately unlock the lower cap the Seller wants.
- **Completion accounts / locked box.** The package refers to "agreed price mechanics" without specifying. Confirm which mechanism applies and that Riverlark, bonuses (+ on-costs), Ironquay AUD 180k and any Sandbar prepayments are expressly listed as debt-like / leakage items.
- **Material adverse change / termination right** between signing and Completion, given Bluefen and the DD-006 incident.
- **Gap covenants** restricting conduct of business, new commitments and any dealing with Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay or the regulator without Buyer consent.
- **Restraints** on Harbourglass and key principals – not mentioned anywhere in the Seller package.

**Bottom line:** the limitation package is drafted so that the Seller's own disclosed problems – a 30%-of-revenue customer consent not obtained, AUD 3.2m of secured debt not discharged, IP the Company does not yet own, AUD 420k+ of Completion-triggered liabilities, and a potentially notifiable privacy breach – would all be disclosed, deemed known, and either unclaimable or subject to a 20% cap and 18-month tail. Each of those items needs to be converted into a Completion deliverable, price adjustment or specific indemnity sitting outside the general regime, and the general regime itself needs the carve-outs above. I would recommend the covering response state plainly that Wattlebridge does not accept the pre-categorisation and treats every clause as open.
